#4332. 10 Games to Play If You Loved Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake

Covering the video games industry since 2017, with experience in news, articles, and reviews. Currently a writer at DualShockers and gaming magazines.

There are few things worse than finishing a fantastic adventure and realizing you have no idea what to play next. With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake arriving earlier this month, plenty of players are probably reaching that bittersweet moment already!

After spending hours exploring Hyrule, solving puzzles, and facing some of gaming's most memorable bosses, it's only natural to feel a little lost when the credits finally roll. But don't worry, because I'm here to help you find your next adventure.

While no game can truly replace the feeling of playing Ocarina of Time for the first time, there are plenty of experiences out there that capture some of the same magic. Whether it's a mysterious world waiting to be explored, clever dungeons, unforgettable characters, or a story that stays with you long after you've put the controller down, there's something on this list for every kind of Zelda fan.

So, if you're already missing Hyrule and aren't quite ready to say goodbye to that feeling of adventure, here are 10 games worth checking out. Some might remind you of classic Zelda, while others take those familiar ideas in completely different directions. Either way, I think you'll find something worth getting lost in!

Nothing beats dealing with the sadness of finishing a fantastic game by jumping straight into its sequel, right? That's why we're kicking things off with Majora's Mask, the final Zelda entry released on the Nintendo 64 and one of the darkest adventures in the entire franchise.

Although it reuses plenty of assets and the basic gameplay of Ocarina of Time, Majora's has an entirely different atmosphere. There's no Triforce, no Princess Zelda to rescue, and no Ganondorf plotting to take over Hyrule. Instead, a mysterious moon is about to crash into the town of Termina, and Link happens to have his Ocarina stolen by the mischievous creature responsible for the whole mess – then, well, someone has to save the day!

This leads to one of the most fascinating mechanics in the series: a three-day time loop that has you traveling through time, helping eccentric characters, and learning the daily schedules of the town's residents. Interestingly, the Ocarina of Time remake actually brings a little more of that NPC schedule system into its own villages, making this sequel feel like a particularly natural follow-up.

If you love the combination of dungeons, memorable boss fights, unusual mechanics, and, of course, a lovely talking companion, then Okami should be right up your alley.

With a structure heavily inspired by classic Zelda adventures, this is one of Capcom's most beloved games, and its story draws heavily from Japanese folklore, following Amaterasu, the sun goddess who takes the form of a white wolf. She must restore life to a land plagued by an ancient evil, beginning with a legendary eight-headed demon that was sealed away a hundred years earlier. Gods, broken seals, spirits, and a spreading darkness? Yeah, I think that should ring a bell for anyone familiar with Hyrule.

It's a perfect pick if you're craving another Zelda-like adventure, and the upcoming sequel gives you one more reason to fall in love with this world.

Mina the Hollower takes place in a world filled with talking skeletons and every kind of magical fantasy you can imagine. So, if the Ocarina of Time left you craving another adventure packed with charming characters and a wonderfully imaginative world, this little indie game might be exactly what you're looking for.

This is a 2D action-adventure with roots deeply tied to some of the most iconic games in the genre – and yes, The Legend of Zelda is definitely one of its biggest inspirations. Between its top-down perspective, exploration, combat, and dungeon-like challenges, you'll probably catch some familiar vibes from the original Zelda and A Link to the Past along the way.

What I particularly love, though, is how Mina the Hollower manages to feel like a love letter to those classics without simply copying them. Its unique story and charming gothic aesthetic give it an identity of its own.

From hearing the iconic Zelda theme again to facing Dark Link and climbing Ganon's Tower, these 10 moments brought back the childhood magic of Ocarina of Time.

If one of the things that stayed with you after playing Ocarina of Time was its bittersweet take on growing up and letting go of the past, then Shadow of the Colossus is an excellent next stop.

This is a much quieter and more melancholic adventure, but it shares that ability to make you feel like you're part of something much bigger than yourself. Instead of exploring villages and dungeons, you'll travel across an enormous, almost deserted landscape on horseback, searching for sixteen colossal creatures. And each encounter is essentially a puzzle of its own, requiring you to figure out how to climb these mysterious beings and find their weak points before delivering the final blow.

And trust me, there's something incredibly special about the atmosphere here! Much like Zelda, the world invites you to explore and take in its surroundings, but there's a sadness lingering beneath all that beauty. If you're looking for another adventure that makes you stop and think about the things we leave behind, this one is hard to beat.

I mean, just look at Tunic’s cover! Do I need to say more? Jokes aside, this lovely indie adventure is another love letter to classic Zelda titles, and what I love most about it is how it perfectly understands the feeling of trusting players to let them figure things out for themselves.

So if you loved the sense of discovery in Ocarina of Time, you're going to feel right at home here! Besides, you play as a little fox exploring a beautifully crafted world filled with hidden passages, dangerous enemies, challenging bosses, and secrets that often require a second look.

Also, Tunic makes exploration feel rewarding in a way that goes beyond simply finding another collectible. Even the game's instruction manual becomes part of the adventure, encouraging you to piece together its mysteries as you go! It's a lovely reminder of why discovering something on your own can be so much more exciting than having the game explain it to you.

If you're still craving that classic Zelda combination of dungeons, clever puzzles, memorable boss fights, and ingenious equipment, Death's Door deserves a spot on your list. It's another indie adventure with a strong love for the genre, but it manages to give those familiar ingredients a personality of its own.

You play as a little crow working as a reaper, collecting souls in a strange world where death has become an increasingly complicated business. Along the way, you'll explore interconnected areas and face some genuinely challenging enemies. The combat is also fast and satisfying, while its dungeons offer plenty of clever environmental puzzles.

What really brings everything together, though, is the atmosphere. The world is wonderfully quirky, the soundtrack is fantastic, and there's a surprising amount of heart beneath its dark humor. It might not be Hyrule, but I think any Zelda fan looking for another compact adventure full of secrets and memorable encounters will have a great time here.

Nintendo changed many things in the Ocarina of Time Remake, big and small, so many of these changes you might not have even noticed.

Sometimes, all you need after finishing a Zelda title is another gorgeous fantasy world to get lost in. And that's exactly what Kena: Bridge of Spirits offers. Its colorful environments and charming characters almost look like they've been pulled straight out of an animated movie, making it an easy recommendation if you loved the magical atmosphere of Ocarina of Time.

But don't let the adorable presentation fool you, though. Kena's combat can get surprisingly challenging, especially when you face some of its larger bosses! Around here, you play as a spirit guide traveling through a beautiful but corrupted land, helping lost souls move on while uncovering the story behind the world around her.

This means that exploration is a big part of the experience, with environmental puzzles and little companions called Rot helping you interact with your surroundings. So there’s a little bit of everything, and it is quite easy to get lost in it!

Sure, most titles on this list are modern games because they're more accessible, but I remember that, back in the day, when I got the post-Ocarina of Time blues, it was Banjo-Tooie that saved me from the heartbreak.

Developed by Rare, this classic platformer takes the colorful gameplay of its predecessor (although you don't need to play the first game to enjoy this one) and expands it into a much bigger experience, with enormous interconnected worlds and plenty of secrets to uncover. There's just a lot to discover in each area, and the way different worlds connect makes exploration particularly rewarding.

It's obviously a different kind of adventure from Zelda, leaning more heavily into 3D platforming, but there's something very familiar about the joy of exploring every corner of its environments. Plus, Banjo-Tooie has plenty of that same old-school magic.

Those who have played the original Ocarina of TIme have made quite a number of mistakes after jumping into The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

One of the things I love most about Zelda is how its adventures can feel both fantastical and surprisingly emotional. If you're looking for another series that combines an imaginative world with a story about friendship, destiny, and growing up, Kingdom Hearts is definitely worth your time.

And the 1.5 + 2.5 ReMIX collection is a great way to experience several important entries in the series and completely immerse yourself in this universe. Okay, maybe I'm cheating a little here, but we're in the middle of a new GTA era, so let me have this one!

Of course, I should also warn you that Kingdom Hearts has a much more confusing story than your average Zelda adventure. But underneath all those twists and mysterious characters is a genuinely heartfelt journey about the bonds we create and the people we want to protect.

Okay, hear me out: even though Metroid Prime Remastered is a first-person sci-fi adventure, it has more in common with Zelda than you might initially expect. In fact, its exploration structure is practically built around the same kind of progression that makes classic Zelda games so satisfying! If you loved finding a new item in Ocarina of Time and immediately wondering which previously inaccessible areas you could now explore, you'll understand what I mean.

Playing as Samus Aran, you'll explore the interconnected regions of the planet Tallon IV, scanning your surroundings and uncovering the mysteries of an ancient civilization. As you acquire new upgrades and abilities, paths that were previously blocked suddenly become accessible, encouraging you to revisit familiar locations with a fresh perspective.

The biggest difference is that you're doing all of this through a first-person perspective, with a much stronger emphasis on shooting and atmospheric exploration. But the satisfaction of gradually understanding how the world fits together is pure Zelda – a lovely reminder that a great adventure doesn't need to take place in Hyrule to capture that same magic.

A tapestry hidden in Ocarina of Time's remake depicts Link's journey before it begins, sparking fan theories about Zelda lore and future games.

Unfortunately, for as much as the changes in 1.1.3.0 have been well received, the launch has been marred by a series of technical issues, some of which are a little unusual.

Immediately after patch 1.1.3.0 went live, players on PC started reporting massive stutters that would occur every few seconds. The issue is especially pronounced in Redsec Battle Royale, but much deadlier in traditional multiplayer.

Battlefield Studios quickly acknowledged it, pointing out a workaround that appears to be working for players on Steam. According to those players, going offline on Steam’s friends menu has fixed stuttering for them.

Perhaps the most disrupting problem the patch has caused is one that prevents players from being able to interact with the game’s menu. Tiles become unresponsive, or outright unselectable when you try to hover near them.

Ironically, the top set of tiles designed to make it easy for players to quickly jump into the new content has been the most affected. Restarting the game sometimes fixes the issue, and some players report that it only happens upon first launch after installing the update.

But Battlefield Studios later clarified that, unsurprisingly, there’s an actual reason behind the bug. Once again, a fix is being investigated, and the developer will offer an update once some progress has been made.

A little further down the list of importance is an issue that stops players from being able to skip tiers within the new Winter Offensive bonus path in the game’s battle pass. This is all a shame to see. Outside of all the problems, the meat of the new update has been almost universally praised. The visibility improvements, and netcode updates have been celebrated. Many players were also happy to see meaningful updates to footstep audio and overall clarity.

It’s also unusual for a Battlefield 6 patch to run into so many issues at launch. The sentiment around 1.1.3.0 so far is that it’s the game’s best and worst update yet. Hopefully those issues will be fixed before the development team breaks for the holidays.

#4328. This remarkable new material could solve a major carbon capture problem

A newly developed material from Oregon State University could help solve one of the biggest challenges in industrial carbon capture: removing carbon dioxide from emissions that contain large amounts of water vapor. Instead of allowing moisture to interfere with the process, the material uses it to help maintain effective carbon capture.

The researchers have filed a patent application for the innovation, which belongs to a class of materials known as metal-organic frameworks, or MOFs. Their findings, published in Angewandte Chemie, could help make carbon capture more practical and affordable for factories and other industrial facilities.

The advance could have important implications for reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Industrial operations, including the burning of fossil fuels to produce energy, are major sources of atmospheric carbon dioxide. In the United States, industry accounts for 30% of total greenhouse gas emissions, according to the Environmental Protection Agency.

A New Material That Overcomes a Major Carbon Capture Problem

The new material, called BVR-X, has an unusual internal structure that keeps water and carbon dioxide largely separated within its microscopic pores. By directing the two substances into different regions, it prevents water molecules from occupying the spaces needed to capture carbon dioxide.

"This internal organization helps the material work under conditions that more closely resemble real industrial emissions," said Kyriakos Stylianou, professor of chemistry in the OSU College of Science.

MOFs are crystalline materials built from positively charged metal ions connected by organic molecules called ligands, which act as linkers. The metal ions form connection points, or nodes, while the linkers join them together into repeating structures resembling tiny cages. These structures contain extremely small pores that can trap gas molecules on their internal surfaces through a process called adsorption, much like a sponge holds substances within its structure.

One of the advantages of MOFs is their remarkable adaptability. Scientists can combine different metals and organic linkers to create materials with specific characteristics. According to Stylianou, millions of MOF designs are theoretically possible. Researchers have already synthesized more than 100,000 distinct MOFs and predicted the properties of hundreds of thousands more.

Why Carbon Capture Needs Better Materials

"The capture of CO2 is critical for meeting net-zero emission targets," said Stylianou, who directs OSU's Materials Discovery Laboratory, known as the MaD Lab. "MOFs have shown a lot of promise because of their porosity and their structural versatility."

Carbon dioxide is a major greenhouse gas released when fossil fuels are burned. As it accumulates in the atmosphere, it traps heat and contributes to global warming.

One approach to addressing the problem involves removing carbon dioxide directly from the atmosphere. Facilities designed for this purpose are beginning to operate in different parts of the world. The world's largest such plant opened in Iceland in 2024, although its annual carbon removal capacity is still relatively small compared with global emissions. According to Stylianou, the facility can capture roughly as much carbon dioxide in one year as about 7,200 cars produce over the same period.

Capturing carbon dioxide before it reaches the atmosphere is another option, and the technologies used for this purpose are considerably more established. At factories and power plants, carbon capture systems can intercept emissions as they travel through exhaust systems and smokestacks. Some of these systems use MOFs to adsorb carbon dioxide molecules from the passing gases.

How Water Makes Industrial Carbon Capture Difficult

A major obstacle, however, is that industrial exhaust often contains substantial amounts of water vapor. Many MOFs that perform well in controlled laboratory experiments lose much of their carbon capture ability when exposed to the humid conditions found in actual smokestacks.

The gases can be dried before carbon dioxide is removed, but doing so requires additional equipment and energy. Those costs can become so significant that the overall process is no longer economically practical for industrial use.

BVR-X offers a different approach. Rather than requiring moisture to be removed, the material responds to water in a way that preserves its ability to collect carbon dioxide. Its internal organization allows water and carbon dioxide to occupy different regions, helping prevent the competition that normally undermines carbon capture performance.

"Water usually makes capturing carbon dioxide more difficult," he said. "Our new material does something unusual: It responds to water by changing in a way that lets it keep capturing CO2 effectively even under very humid conditions."

Strong Performance Under Realistic Industrial Conditions

Laboratory tests demonstrated that BVR-X could efficiently capture carbon dioxide from a highly humid gas stream containing only 4% carbon dioxide.

That concentration is particularly relevant to emissions from burning natural gas, where carbon dioxide makes up a relatively small proportion of the exhaust. Extracting it becomes especially difficult when large quantities of water vapor are also present.

The experiments therefore tested the material under conditions that resemble an important real-world challenge, "where separating a small amount of CO2 in the presence of substantial water is particularly challenging," said Stylianou.

The researchers also found that BVR-X could repeatedly capture and release carbon dioxide without losing its effectiveness over dozens of cycles. This ability to regenerate the material is important because commercial carbon capture systems must reuse their capture materials many times to keep operating costs manageable.

"And the material can be regenerated and reused, maintaining performance through dozens of capture-and-release cycles and tolerating demanding conditions," he added. "Those are important qualities for practical carbon-capture technologies."

The results suggest that BVR-X could help overcome a major limitation of existing MOF technologies, particularly in industrial settings where removing moisture from exhaust gases would otherwise be costly.

The study brought together researchers from several institutions. Stylianou worked with MaD Lab members Ankit Yadav, Emmanuel Musa and Andrzej Gładysiak, along with Micah Hickethier, Chun-Wai Chang and Kai Shen Choong from the Oregon State College of Engineering.

Additional collaborators included scientists from the University of California, Berkeley; the University of Oregon; and the ARAMCO Research and Development Center.

Funding was provided by Saudi Aramco, the Murdock Charitable Trust, and a donor-advised fund established by Oregon State University alumni and retired public school teachers Brian and Marilyn Kleiner through the OSU Foundation.

#4327. Ferrari 296 Challenge Stradale Is the Purest Prancing Horse in Years

The 296 CS adds serious aero and ditches the GTB's hybrid system for a more enthusiast-focused driving experience.

Nostalgia must be in the air in Maranello. A few months ago, Ferrari unveiled the 12Cilindri Manuale, reintroducing a (simulated) six-speed manual transmission to its model lineup purely for the sake of driver involvement. And now, the Challenge Stradale badge returns to the rear engine mesh of a Prancing Horse for the first time since the 360 CS was discontinued in 2004. Simply put, it's a good year to be a sentimental Ferrarista.

In the same vein as its predecessor, the 296 Challenge Stradale is a road car that shares its fundamental philosophy with the new 296 Challenge Evo racecar, which will debut in the single-marque Ferrari Challenge racing series next year. Parked side by side at their reveal at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya today, we would excuse a gentleman driver for confusing the CS with his new track-only machinery.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 51503

There have been several limited-edition, track-focused mid-engine Ferraris since the 360 Challenge Stradale—including the F430 Scuderia, 458 Speciale, and 488 Pista—but the 296 Challenge Stradale goes the furthest of all of them in emulating its racecar counterpart, both aesthetically and mechanically.

While previous track-centric Ferraris have been somewhat demurely styled, the 296 CS puts its aerodynamic elements on full display. The carbon-fiber rear wing, dive planes, adjustable front splitter, and vented hood are essentially a copy-paste job from the Challenge Evo, with concessions made for road legality. Up front, twin vents positioned in the hood just before the windshield channel hot air expelled from two under-hood radiators over the windshield and towards the rear of the car, reducing the aerodynamic variations caused by changing ground clearance.

Other aero features are hidden out of sight. The CS's underbody has been smoothed to better feed the rear diffuser and work with three pairs of vortex generators at the front and two at the rear to generate additional downforce. With all of the aerodynamic elements colluding, the 296 Challenge Stradale makes 1360 pounds of downforce at 155 mph. That's a 72-percent increase over the base 296GTB's peak figure.

Big changes have been made to the CS's powertrain. You won't find any orange high-voltage wiring snaking around under the glass of its mid-mounted hood like you would in a 296GTB or 296 Speciale, as the 5-kWh battery pack and rear-mounted axial-flux electric motor have been removed entirely. The twin-turbo 3.0-liter V-6 operates unassisted and supposedly sounds better than ever courtesy of a reworked twin-exit exhaust system.

See all results for Ferrari 296 for sale near 51503

Overall firepower has decreased to 670 horsepower—149 ponies less than the standard 296GTB's. The upside is a notable decrease in mass, with Ferrari claiming that the removal of the plug-in-hybrid componentry played a major role in shedding 328 pounds from the 296GTB's dry weight. A lightened transmission flex plate, driveshaft, and timing cover were also developed to make the CS's powertrain as featherweight as possible. Without an electric motor present to fill in any thrust gaps left by turbo lag, the V-6 has been retuned to increase low-end grunt, although peak torque remains 546 pound-feet delivered at 8250 rpm.

As to be expected, yanking out an integrated powertrain system comes with some unique challenges that affect more than just the engine itself. For example, Ferrari was forced to enlarge the 296 CS's rear carbon-ceramic brake discs and the ventilation ducts that cool them to compensate for the lack of regenerative braking. The decreased weight in the rear also shifted its weight distribution 1.5 percent to the front, which was addressed with suspension design and geometry changes.

The CS's newly developed suspension is derived directly from the 296 Challenge Evo and features semi-active dampers and a dual-spring design that improves rebound response. The result is reduced body roll, which helps the performance of the specially developed Pirelli P Zero R tires, measuring 245/35R20 in the front and 305/35R20 in the rear. The 20-inch forged wheels can be ordered in Matte Grigio Corsa, Matte Nero with a diamond-cut finish, or Matte Bianco Fuji.

The 296 Challenge Stradale's cockpit is very similar to the one found in the 296 Speciale. While niceties like climate control and a stereo remain, carbon-fiber door panels and a lack of armrests and storage pockets are a clear indication of the CS's weight-saving mission. For true gluttons for punishment, an even further stripped interior spec is available that removes the trim from the area beneath the seats and the lower section of the carpets beneath the center console, leaving part of the chassis exposed.

Ferrari is adamant that the 296 CS isn't a replacement for the 296 Speciale and will not cannibalize that model's customer base, as the two are intended for different buyers. Besides being geared less towards outright track duty, the 296 Speciale is a part of Ferrari's special series, meaning that customers need to have an "existing relationship" with the brand in order to get an allocation. The 296 Challenge Stradale is a standard range model, meaning anyone can walk into a dealer and order one, existing relationship or not. Ferrari says that it wants to court new Ferrari buyers interested in experiencing the purest driving experience that the prancing horse has to offer, and the 296 CS is the first step in that direction.

U.S. pricing has not been announced, but in its home market, the 296 Challenge Stradale costs 291,000 euros, or the equivalent of about $320,000. Stateside deliveries of the new CS are expected to begin sometime in late 2027. As a non-Speciale model, CS production numbers aren’t limited, which presents a unique opportunity to buy a special new Ferrari without already owning one.

The time has arrived for another Arc Raiders update, and Embark has certainly delivered. Today’s patch, version 1.6.0, is among the smallest the game has received so far, focusing almost exclusively on disabling map exploits.

Perhaps more important than the patch itself, however, is the announcement the developer made around it.

Starting off with patch 1.6.0, it takes out a particular zipline on Stella Montis, the game’s most recent addition ot the map roster. Some players used said zipline to get out of bounds, something the game has been battling on several of its maps.

On Blue Gate, the patch fixes a collision issue that allowed players to vault through a wall, and fall to their death. The map fixes continue with another on Spaceport Launch Tower, which takes out a gap in collision that players have been able to shoot through.

The last change in this update affects gameplay feel around Arc enemies. Certain materials in the game’s world weren’t blocking their vision - or fire - when they should have, and this has now been fixed.

Alongside today’s patch, Embark also announced that going forward, we’re going to see fewer patches for Arc Raiders. The game has been getting updates almost every Thursday since it launched in late October.

Now that most of the major problems have been fixed, the studio is shifting to a slower patching cadence. Critical fixes will still be issued as soon as they’re developed, but don’t expect a patch each week going forward.

Embark also revealed that patch releases and in-game store rotations will now occur on Tuesdays. You should also expect the next few weeks to be quiet, as members of the team go on holiday breaks.

But, before everyone goes away, the game is going to get one more big update. The last item on Arc Raiders’ roadmap, revealed in early November, is the Cold Snap event. This is on track for Tuesday, bringing some new content alongside a few other fixes.

#4325. Why obesity affects men and women differently may be hiding in their fat

Scientists at the University of California, Riverside have uncovered a surprising difference in how the immune systems of males and females respond to obesity. Their findings suggest that certain immune cells found in body fat can help protect against inflammation and metabolic problems, while others may make these harmful effects worse.

The discovery centers on eosinophils, immune cells best known for their involvement in allergies and asthma. In experiments with mice, researchers found that these cells behave differently depending on biological sex, potentially helping explain why obesity does not affect males and females in the same way.

The study, published in PNAS Nexus, was led by University of California, Riverside biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik. Their findings challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar cells with relatively few specialized functions. The results also point toward potential new approaches for treating obesity and its complications.

Six Types of Immune Cells Found in Body Fat

To investigate the role of eosinophils in obesity, the researchers used high-resolution single-cell sequencing, a technique that allows scientists to examine gene activity in individual cells. They identified six distinct eosinophil populations in adipose (fat) tissue, each with its own pattern of gene expression and potentially different biological functions.

This unexpected diversity suggests that eosinophils play a much more complicated role in metabolic health than previously recognized.

"Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought," said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences in the UCR School of Medicine. "Some populations can protect against obesity, and if we can identify and activate the pathways that produce these protective cells, we may find new ways to improve metabolic health."

Why Male and Female Fat Tissue Respond Differently

One of the most striking discoveries was a difference in the immune cells found in male and female mice.

Female mice possessed a protective population of eosinophils that appeared to communicate more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells present in fat tissue. According to Nair, this cooperation may help create a healthier environment within fat tissue and support better metabolic function.

Male mice showed a different pattern. When given a diet high in fat, they were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation. Their fat tissue also contained eosinophils with gene activity patterns suggesting weaker protective functions.

These findings indicate that the effects of eosinophils on obesity depend on more than simply how many of these cells are present. The particular type of eosinophil and its interactions with neighboring immune cells may be equally important.

"This means the relationship between eosinophils and obesity is not simply a matter of how many eosinophils are present," said Rebecca E. Ruggiero-Ruff, a postdoctoral researcher in Nair's lab and co-first author of the paper. "Their functional characteristics and how they communicate with other immune cells are also critical."

A Protein That May Help Protect Against Inflammation

The researchers also identified a protein called RELM alpha that appears to play an important role in maintaining the beneficial relationship between eosinophils and macrophages.

Produced by macrophages, RELM alpha seemed to help stabilize communication between the two immune cell types in female mice. This interaction may be one reason certain eosinophil populations are better able to support healthy fat tissue.

The finding builds on earlier experiments by the same research group, which showed that administering RELM alpha to mice produced protective effects. Together, the results suggest that the protein may help regulate immune activity within fat tissue and influence how the body responds to obesity.

Could the Discovery Lead to Better Obesity Treatments?

Although the results offer new insight into the biology of obesity, the experiments were conducted in mice. Researchers have also detected eosinophils in fat tissue from people with obesity, but scientists do not yet fully understand what these cells do in the human body.

Nair cautioned that additional research will be necessary before the discovery can be used to develop treatments. One particularly important question is whether therapies targeting the immune system would work differently in men and women.

"A drug may not activate the same pathways or produce the same effects in males and females, particularly when it targets the immune system," said co-first author Xinru Qiu, a postdoctoral researcher in Godzik's lab. "We need to investigate sex-specific biology more thoroughly so that treatments can be optimized for different patients."

Understanding these differences could eventually help researchers design more personalized treatments for obesity and the metabolic complications associated with it.

Scientists Plan to Recreate Human Fat Tissue in the Lab

The research team is now investigating whether the protective behavior observed in mouse eosinophils can also be studied in human laboratory models.

To accomplish this, the scientists are developing three-dimensional adipose organoids. These miniature laboratory models reproduce certain features of real fat tissue, allowing researchers to examine how eosinophils interact with fat cells and other components of their environment.

The goal is to determine whether changing communication between immune cells could encourage healthier responses in human fat tissue.

"We ultimately hope to develop human adipose organoids that will allow us to investigate whether manipulating immune-cell communication can promote healthier tissue responses," said Godzik, a professor of biomedical sciences and the Bruce D. and Nancy B. Varner Presidential Endowed Chair in Cancer Research.

The findings raise the possibility that targeting specific immune cell populations, rather than treating all eosinophils as functionally identical, could eventually provide new ways to address obesity and its complications. Whether the same protective mechanisms operate in humans remains an important question for future research.

The research team also included Lauren Vance, Yuxin He, and Djurdjica Coss, who worked alongside Nair, Godzik, Ruggiero-Ruff, and Qiu.

Funding for the study came from the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine, and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine.

The research paper is titled "Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity."

#4323. GTA 6 May Have Cost $1 Billion, But It Has Paid Itself Off Three Times Over

Scott Baird is a Contributor from the UK with over a decade of video game writing experience.

Grand Theft Auto 6 cost a lot of money to make, but Rockstar and Take-Two’s gamble paid off, bringing in three times its initial billion-dollar budget.

Fans of the Grand Theft Auto franchise were frustrated by the numerous delays and gaps in announcements for the sixth entry in the franchise. While many believed this was a positive sign, as it proved Rockstar wasn’t going to run the game out the door, it also led to speculation about a project that was facing troubles behind the scenes, like many titles before it.

On November 19, 2026, Grand Theft Auto 6 finally launched, and many people were there on day one. The true scope of Grand Theft Auto 6’s success has been revealed by Take-Two in a statement to Variety, revealing just how much money the game has made so far.

According to Take-Two, Grand Theft Auto 6 has made over $3 billion, triple its production budget. The entire day-one take (including pre-orders) was 32.5 million units sold, making it the single biggest entertainment launch of all time and beating anything produced by big names like Minecraft, Star Wars, Marvel, or Harry Potter.

It is worth mentioning that this is only the console launch for two platforms, as Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently available only on PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series X/S. The PC release in 2027 is also expected to be huge, and if Rockstar can get the game running on the Switch 2, then Nintendo fans can join in too.

There’s also the future to consider, as Grand Theft Auto 6 is having some performance woes on the current hardware. If Rockstar has an enhanced version waiting for the PlayStation 6 and XBOX Project Helix, then that’s even more money coming in. That might take a while, however, as those platforms aren’t expected until 2028 at the earliest, and if hardware prices keep rising, no one will buy them.

The entire day one take (including pre-orders) was 32.5 million units sold, making it the single biggest entertainment launch of all time, beating anything produced by the big names, like Minecraft, Star Wars, Marvel, or Harry Potter.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is currently only a single-player game, which means the inevitable successor to Grand Theft Auto Online is still coming. Grand Theft Auto Online helped propel Grand Theft Auto 5 to the status of the second-best-selling video game of all time, and the same could well happen for its sequel.

It’s safe to say that Rockstar and Take-Two’s multiple delays for Grand Theft Auto 6 paid off. The game could have been rushed out in an incomplete state back in 2025 or 2026, but as Cyberpunk 2077 proved, that can completely ruin a series’ reputation, and Rockstar would have had to work hard to earn it back.

As it stands, Grand Theft Auto 6 is the most highly acclaimed and best-reviewed video game of all time, with relatively few performance issues and glitches at launch. If it had launched in a rough state, that would have tanked the review scores, which will be a huge part of the game’s post-launch ad campaign.

Grand Theft Auto 6 has become the biggest media moment in recent memory, and it’s just getting started. With more platforms and the online mode still on the way, there’s no telling just how far the game will go. Perhaps the time has come for a video game to finally outsell Minecraft, a feat that no one thought possible, but may finally come to pass.

#4320. Scientists create a remarkable new rechargeable battery using vitamin B12

Scientists have found an unexpected new use for vitamin B12, a nutrient best known for its importance to human health. Researchers at the University of Córdoba have incorporated the vitamin into a rechargeable battery, demonstrating for the first time that it can serve as a catalyst in this type of energy storage system.

Vitamin B12 is essential for normal bodily function and is naturally present in animal products. The vitamin is produced by certain bacteria, which occur in nature and are also grown commercially to supply the food and pharmaceutical industries. In addition to its established applications in medicine, nutrition, and veterinary care, B12 is used to address certain nutritional deficiencies. It has also become popular alongside other B vitamins as a hangover remedy because of its potential to help reduce fatigue.

Now, scientists are exploring an entirely different application. By using the vitamin to support the chemical reactions inside a battery, they have developed a prototype capable of completing up to 250 charging and discharging cycles.

How Vitamin B12 Makes a Rechargeable Battery Possible

The new battery was developed by the Physical Chemistry research group (FQM-204) at the University of Córdoba's Chemical Institute for Energy and the Environment (IQUEMA). It uses zinc and oxygen from the surrounding air to produce electricity, with vitamin B12, also called cobalamin, playing a crucial role in the process.

To make the design work, the researchers attached vitamin B12 molecules to single-walled carbon nanotubes. The vitamin contains cobalt (III) at its center, which helps drive the electrochemical reactions needed for the battery to function.

The team has previously experimented with natural molecules as battery catalysts, including hemoglobin and catalase. These substances contain iron (II) and iron (III), respectively. Vitamin B12 represents the group's third effort to use a biological molecule for this purpose, but it has delivered an important advance: a battery that can be recharged repeatedly, completing as many as 250 cycles.

One of the biggest obstacles was keeping vitamin B12 inside the battery. Because the vitamin dissolves readily in water, it would normally be difficult to retain in a system that relies on a water-based electrolyte.

The researchers overcame this problem by securing the vitamin to carbon nanotubes, using an approach inspired by how amino acids connect to form proteins.

Manuel Cano Luna, one of the study's authors, explained that "we looked at the properties we can find in naturally occurring materials to use them in new batteries," while describing the team's search for useful biological compounds.

Their attachment technique imitates "the process by which amino acids bind together in proteins."

Alongside Cano Luna, the research team included Valentín García Caballero, Miguel López León, Pablo Gómez Argudo, Luis Camacho Delgado, José Miguel Rodríguez Mellado, María Teresa Martín Romero, José Abad López, and Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero.

A Safer, Lighter Alternative to Lithium-Ion Batteries

The findings, published in the Journal of Materials Chemistry A, could contribute to the development of battery technologies that depend less on the materials used in conventional lithium-ion batteries.

Although lithium-ion batteries are widely used, obtaining their raw materials can involve significant economic, environmental, and social challenges. Zinc-air batteries offer a potential alternative because they can store substantial amounts of energy relative to their weight while relying on materials that are more readily available.

Zinc is abundant and recyclable, and these batteries use oxygen from the surrounding atmosphere as part of their energy-producing reactions. Because they draw oxygen from the air rather than storing all the necessary reactants internally, they can also be lighter than other battery designs.

This advantage has helped make zinc-air batteries increasingly useful in compact electronic devices, particularly hearing aids. Another benefit is their use of non-flammable, water-based electrolytes, which can reduce fire risks and improve safety.

A major challenge in developing rechargeable zinc-air batteries is finding a catalyst that can efficiently support the chemical reactions involved in both producing and storing electricity.

During discharge, the battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy. Recharging requires the relevant chemical reactions to proceed in the opposite direction. A suitable catalyst must therefore be effective in both processes.

According to researcher Antonio Jesús Fernández Romero, vitamin B12 "has proven to meet the necessary conditions to act as a good catalyst because, during discharge, it catalyzes the reduction of oxygen to water and, during recharging, it promotes the production of oxygen."

This ability to support both reactions is what makes the vitamin particularly promising for rechargeable zinc-air battery technology.

Could Vitamin B12 Help Store Renewable Energy?

The successful prototype offers a new direction for researchers seeking affordable, sustainable alternatives to existing energy storage technologies.

If the approach can be developed further, batteries using vitamin B12 catalysts could eventually help address one of the biggest challenges facing renewable energy: storing excess electricity generated by sources such as solar and wind power for use when production falls.

Although the technology remains at the research stage, demonstrating up to 250 charge and discharge cycles shows that a familiar biological molecule can play an unexpected role in rechargeable battery design. The discovery adds to growing efforts to use naturally occurring substances to create safer, lighter, and more sustainable ways to store energy.

#4317. 10 Best Easter Eggs in GTA 6

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

The most common thing for any game developer to do is to make nods to different franchises in their game. Affectionately called easter eggs, these little details are meant to be surprises for players who love various other franchises.

Whether you are a fan of games, television shows, or movies, there’s plenty to discover in Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar has taken the time to hide trophies all around Leonida for those who are diligent enough to go searching for them. Even 'Weird Al' Yankovic is hiding in this game somewhere.

Have you found Dexter’s apartment? Maybe you have gone searching for the literal easter egg. Either way, these are amazing nods to other franchises in the mighty GTA 6.

Dexter is a very popular television series about a vigilante serial killer. This serial killer just so happens to live in Miami, which just so happens to be the city that Vice City is based on. What a coincidence!

It just so happens that Rockstar noticed this connection and decided to add a few nods to the series in GTA 6, with the first of them being Dexter’s apartment, which is located on Washington Island.

Of course, you won’t be able to reach this area right away, but once you get access to the map, you can head straight there to check it out and pay tribute to the television series. You can also find some tools on the roof.

Bigfoot has decided to make his way out of the northern forests and headed south to the marshlands of Leonida. It’s a bit weird that he decided to make this island paradise his home, but I won’t question that.

If you progress through the story of GTA 6, there is a mission that will set you on the path to discovering Bigfoot, but he is easy to overlook, as he runs away rather quickly once you get near him.

I barely caught a glimpse of him, but chased him down and caught a photo before he mysteriously disappeared into the marsh. I have no idea if I will see him again, but it was cool to catch a glimpse of this mysterious figure.

After Grand Theft Auto 5's release, the Mount Chiliad mystery was one of the most talked about easter eggs out there. Here's what we know today.

Some developers make nods to different games or pop culture, but Rockstar takes the time to put a literal easter egg in its game. That’s right, if you go to the correct spot on the map, you can find a nest with literal easter eggs in it.

The location in question is a radio tower in South Vice Dale County. The radio tower takes multiple minutes to climb, but the payoff is definitely worth it, as you find a nest full of easter eggs at the top.

While I won’t spoil what happens when you throw one, it does involve a cutscene, and you should definitely take the time to visit the location and watch it unfold.

One of the most memorable missions in GTA 5 is when Michael’s boat gets stolen and you need to chase down the people responsible. Unfortunately, Michael’s boat doesn’t get returned, but we now know the whereabouts of it, and it turns out that it landed in Jason’s yard.

Next to Jason’s house, there is a run-down boat that looks similar to Michael’s. People have pointed this out for a while, but there was no confirmation until now.

Since the game is officially out, you can check out the boat, and you can even climb on top of it. Once there, you can use your phone’s camera to check out the display. Doing so will allow you to see a display that shows part of the GTA 5 map, seemingly confirming that this is Michael’s boat.

Have you ever heard of a movie called Island Claws? If not, you aren’t the only one, but there is a nod to this film in GTA 6. The movie is from the 1980s, and it is about a scientist who genetically modifies crabs to make them grow larger to solve world hunger.

Unfortunately, this doesn’t work out very well, and a similar thing has transpired in Leonida. In Pelican Valley, you can find a trail of blood that leads to a shack. Inside the shack, you can find information about failed experiments on crabs.

Along with this, Jason will get attacked by a giant crab that jumps down on him from the ceiling. It is a rather large easter egg that is meant to pay homage to the classic independent film. Good job doing your research Rockstar.

One of the things that people loved to do in Grand Theft Auto 5 was break into the military base, and the go-to means of breaking into the base was via the hill jump just outside the fence along the highway.

Well, there is another military base in GTA 6 and it is located near where you start the game. It is called Mile Zero Air Station, and it has a convenient hill just outside the fence that you can use to jump into the base just like in GTA 5.

There is no way that this is a coincidence because the hill is an obvious jumping point. Thank you Rockstar for including an obvious homage to the previous game and the silly antics players got into.

From drawings in a mental hospital to TV and radio commercials, these are nine Rockstar Games Easter Eggs that hint at a shared universe.

The most common meme that has ever been spread about a video game is probably the, “We got [insert item here] before GTA 6.” It popped up every single time something major happened before the release of the game. Well it can’t be said anymore since the game is out.

With that being said, the meme will probably become about either Elder Scrolls 6 or GTA 7, or maybe even RAC 7. You might be wondering what that is. Well, if you scroll through your phone’s Snapmatic app, you can find a post about a game called Barnyard Blue: Hot Pursuit.

The post reads, “Barnyard Blue video game before Race and Chase 7 is crazy.” There is even a comment that reads, “We really got Barnyard Blue games before RAC 7.” This is, of course, a jab at the classic meme that appeared for so many years.

The X-Men actually exist in the Grand Theft Auto universe, except they don’t exist in the same way as you know them. Instead of being called the X-Men, they are referred to as the RX-Men. A strange choice, but one that makes it obvious that it is a reference to the classic hero team.

There are various magazines that you can find in the different convenience stores around Leonida, but you can reliably find this magazine in the 24-7 supermarket in northern Key Lento.

In this story, you can find a copy of RX-Men issue 13 titled, “Paging Dr. Placebo.” It features GTA renditions of different heroes and villains. There’s also collectible cards for these characters sprinkled around Leonida.

Speaking of trading cards, you can find various wrestling trading cards across Leonida. This is an obvious easter egg to the various wrestling trading cards that already exist. The wrestling company is called B.A.M, and it stands for Backyard American Mania.

Florida has a rather large wrestling scene, with the WWE training facility being in Orlando. On top of this, various famous wrestlers live or lived in Florida.

To go even further, the acronym of B.A.M. can also be related to Bird Azarian Memorial Training Center, which is located in Illinois, but is a wrestling training center. Odds are, it is just a reference to WWE wrestling.

Early in the game, Jason and Cal sit down to play some games on the JoyStation, with the system itself being an obvious reference to the PlayStation 5. However, that isn’t the whole easter egg, as the game that is played is called Tenebrae Lux.

Tenebrae Lux is a game themed after the movie called The Lighthouse, which features both Robert Pattinson and Willem Dafoe. This is awesome, but there is yet one more easter egg hidden here.

The name Tenebrae Lux is Latin for the term “light-dark.” This happens to be the exact translation of the French term Clair Obscur, which is one of the greatest games to have been released in recent years and a game that took the world by storm.

This list delves into some of the best Easter eggs in video games, exploring how to unlock them, what they're referencing, and more.

#4316. Scientists discover a hidden hereditary form of aggressive prostate cancer

Scientists have identified a previously unrecognized inherited form of prostate cancer that, although extremely rare, can lead to aggressive disease relatively early in life. The discovery, made by researchers at the University of British Columbia (UBC), could help doctors identify families with a heightened genetic risk and detect cancer before it spreads.

Most cancers develop as genetic changes build up in cells over time. However, approximately 5% to 10% are associated with inherited mutations that can be passed from parents to their children, creating a cancer risk that may extend across generations.

Among the most familiar examples are mutations in the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes. These inherited changes can substantially raise the likelihood of breast, ovarian, pancreatic, and prostate cancers. Testing for BRCA mutations has reshaped cancer prevention and treatment by allowing people with elevated risks to receive earlier screening and preventive care.

Now, a study published in Cancer Discovery points to another gene, CDK12, as a potentially important marker of inherited prostate cancer risk. After examining genetic information from more than 4,500 people with aggressive prostate cancer, the researchers discovered five unrelated men with inherited mutations in CDK12. Every one of these men developed metastatic prostate cancer between ages 44 and 62, meaning the cancer had spread beyond the prostate.

"What's striking is that every patient we identified with this inherited mutation had already developed metastatic disease by the time they were diagnosed," said senior author Dr. Alexander Wyatt, associate professor of urologic sciences in the UBC faculty of medicine and UBC President's Excellence Chair in Precision Oncology. "The opportunity now is to identify these families earlier and give people the chance to benefit from enhanced screening, when there are still curative treatment options."

A Hidden Genetic Cause of Aggressive Prostate Cancer

The discovery challenges a longstanding assumption about CDK12. Scientists previously believed that harmful changes in this gene developed spontaneously inside cancer cells rather than being inherited from a parent.

To investigate whether the inherited mutations were actually contributing to the disease, the team examined the patients' tumors for a distinctive pattern of genetic damage associated with loss of CDK12 function. This molecular fingerprint helped connect the inherited mutations to the development of their cancers.

"The tumors provided us with a genetic signature that pointed directly back to CDK12," said lead author Dr. Sofie Tolmeijer, a postdoctoral fellow in the Wyatt lab. "It gave us compelling evidence that these inherited mutations were playing a direct role in causing their cancer."

The findings emerged from a broad international research effort involving UBC, BC Cancer, the Vancouver Coastal Health Research Institute, and the University of Washington, along with scientists at institutions in Australia, the Netherlands, Spain, and Belgium.

Despite the potentially serious consequences, inherited CDK12 mutations appear to be exceptionally uncommon. The researchers found them in approximately one out of every 1,000 people with aggressive prostate cancer. Even at that low frequency, they estimate that hundreds of families around the world could be affected.

"While this mutation is extremely rare, the discovery could be lifesaving for the families who carry it," said Dr. Tolmeijer. "Finding one person with an inherited mutation gives us the opportunity to identify other family members at risk and help them take action before cancer develops or spreads."

Genetic Testing Could Help Detect Prostate Cancer Earlier

One of the most promising implications of the discovery is that doctors may not need to develop entirely new testing technology to put the findings into practice.

The researchers recommend including CDK12 in standard genetic testing panels used to assess hereditary prostate cancer risk. These panels examine multiple genes associated with inherited cancer susceptibility, helping identify individuals who may benefit from closer medical monitoring.

Importantly, the clinical technology required to detect CDK12 mutations already exists. That could make expanding genetic testing relatively straightforward, potentially reducing the time and expense needed to bring the discovery into routine patient care.

"One of the most exciting aspects of this discovery is that we already have the technology needed to act on it," said Dr. Wyatt, who is also a senior research scientist at the Vancouver Prostate Centre and senior scientist at BC Cancer. "Adding CDK12 to existing genetic tests is relatively straightforward, which means this discovery could move from the research lab into clinical care much more quickly."

Could the Same Mutation Increase Ovarian Cancer Risk?

The study also uncovered clues suggesting that inherited CDK12 mutations might be associated with ovarian cancer, although more research is needed to establish whether they increase the risk.

Several of the men with inherited CDK12 mutations had relatives with a history of ovarian cancer. The investigators also identified another person who had ovarian cancer and carried an inherited CDK12 mutation. Analysis of that person's tumor revealed the same characteristic genetic signature seen in the prostate cancer cases.

Together, these observations suggest that CDK12 could potentially play a role in hereditary cancer risk beyond the prostate. Further studies will be needed to determine how strongly the mutations are associated with ovarian cancer and whether they should influence screening recommendations.

For families carrying these rare mutations, the potential benefits of identifying their genetic risk could be substantial. Earlier testing may give relatives the opportunity to receive closer surveillance and, if cancer develops, begin treatment before it reaches an advanced stage.

"With the right genetic testing and screening programs, we envision a future where no one who inherits one of these mutations dies from cancer," said Dr. Wyatt.

The research received funding from the Prostate Cancer Foundation, Terry Fox Research Institute, Canadian Cancer Society, Canadian Institutes of Health Research, Michael Smith Health Research BC, U.S. National Institutes of Health, BC Cancer Foundation, and other funding partners.

Materials provided by University of British Columbia. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4315. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4314. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. #4312. GTA 6: Best Starter Car to Register

Christian Bognar is a Contributor at DualShockers with over three years of experience covering the gaming industry. Since 2022, he has written guides and reviews for publications including DualShockers, CBR, Attack of the Fanboy, PC Invasion, and The Game Slayer. He holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration

During your Grand Theft Auto 6 playthrough, you will eventually get the opportunity to register a car. Registering cars allows you to call them easily from your phone with a small BuckMe fee.

This opportunity comes at the start of Chapter 2, where you learn about a man named Moses who deals with stolen cars. To unlock Moses and his shop for good, you need to bring him your very first car to register.

Instead of stealing the coolest car to register, I recommend going a different route. Here’s the best starter car to register in GTA 6.

During the first mission of Chapter 2 in GTA 6, you will naturally meet a girl named Vicki. During this mission, Vicki will eventually mention Moses to Lucia, and once she does, Moses shop will be marked on the map with the objective to bring him a starter car to register.

Find the red Phoenix in GTA 6’s Unwanted Attention mission, sneak through the police impound, escape the cops, and deliver the car to Brian.

After bringing Moses one car and registering it with him for free, you will unlock the ability to register most cars in Leonida. The only cars you can’t register with Moses are the ones with trackers, so make a mental note of that.

Also, keep in mind that even though you can register your starter car for free, registering every other car from here on out will cost you money. The price of registration depends on the type of car.

While players may want to steal and register the flashiest car in Leonida as their starter, this isn’t necessarily the smartest move. The nice sports cars won’t have the most trunk space and can be hard to control.

Instead, it would be best to choose a pickup truck for a starter car, as they have a ton of stash space and are generally easy to drive.

Find GTA 6 Ultimate Edition vehicles, weapons, clothing, and hairstyles, and learn which chapters and locations unlock each item.

It may seem unimportant, but having more stash space will allow Lucia to transport more money and robbery loot on a single trip. This means you can gather money faster, without constantly needing to visit ATMs.

Additionally, as previously mentioned, pickup trucks are generally on the easier side to control when driving. This is important early in the game since it will allow you to have an easier time exploring, crashing less, and avoiding the need to pay for repairs.

Once you've built up wealth by using your starter car as a getaway and stash for loot from robberies and muggings, you can use any extra cash to register nicer vehicles.

Simply put, the coolest cars tend to have the highest registration price, so you want a reliable one that will help you get around easier and stash more money to start off.

Find a tank at Mile Zero Air Station in GTA 6. Learn where to enter the base, where the tanks are parked, and what to expect when you escape.

While there are many pickup trucks to find across the map of GTA VI, I have had the best luck finding them in parking lots. More specifically, I have found pickup trucks commonly in parking lots in front of bars, clothing shops, barbershops, etc.

In other words, pickup trucks are very easy to find, considering they aren’t that special when it comes to style and speed and aren’t considered “rare.” If you are worried about finding one in a specific color, you shouldn’t be, considering Moses makes you change the color when you bring it in.

Once you find a pickup truck (or a different car if you decided not to listen to my advice), bring it on over to Moses and tell him you’d like to register it.

After the quick transaction with Moses is complete, you are now able to call your starter car to your location whenever you like for a small BuckMe price via the Scooter Bros app on your phone.

#4311. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4309. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.
